summary: Heart rate leads, pace follows. HR <=158 to the half, <=160 to km 30, then race. Two 160 mL honey flasks (~100 g carbs each) = 8 sips tied to aid stations, water at every station, 500 mL backup water in the vest. Start 50-100 m behind the 3:15 pacer.
goldenRules: Obey whichever ceiling you hit first: HR ceiling or pace ceiling. Low HR is not permission to run faster than the pace ceiling before km 30.
Never chase lost time with a surge. Run the target pace from where you are; the gap closes by itself.
Judge HR on the km-lap average, not on a single reading. Ignore spikes on bridges, underpasses and at aid stations.
Lanes only move down (or stay) before km 30. No climbing back up.
Every honey sip is followed by water from a cup. Water at every station, sip or not.
Use the official km markers for splits, not watch distance (the watch will read 0.3-0.5 km long).

lanes.name: A-stretch
lanes.when: km 10 lap at 4:33-4:38 with lap-avg HR <=155, legs light, short sentences possible. Close on the 3:15 pacer.

lanes.name: A-real
lanes.when: HR 156-158 at 4:38-4:40. What the HR rule should actually produce. Keep the pacer in sight, don't chase.

lanes.name: B
lanes.when: HR >158 at 4:40+ by km 10, heavy legs or gut trouble early, or HR >160 at the half.

lanes.name: C - survival
lanes.when: HR >165 at the same pace, pace fading >10 s/km at the same HR, cramp or light-headedness. Banana at 31.5, walk 10 s through each station, keep running to the line.

phases.note: Adrenaline inflates HR. Start 50-100 m behind the 3:15 pacer.
Settle. First honey sip at km 6.
Cruise in the pack. Fuel exactly on schedule.
+2 bpm of normal drift allowed. Do not speed up yet.
First place you are allowed to push - only if the km 30 check is green.
Coke at 39.5. Empty the tank from km 40.

overCapProtocol.trigger: Lap-avg HR 1-2 bpm over the ceiling
overCapProtocol.action: Ease 5 s/km. Give it 1 km - HR lags 60-90 s behind a pace change.
Ease 10 s/km (from your data ~3-4 s/km is worth 1 bpm).

overCapProtocol.trigger: Still over after 2 km of easing
overCapProtocol.action: Drop one lane (A-stretch -> A-real -> B). No climbing back before km 30.
Straight to B (4:45-4:50). Check you didn't miss a honey sip or water.

overCapProtocol.trigger: HR 5+ bpm UNDER the expected band at target pace
overCapProtocol.action: You may go 5 s/km faster - never faster than the pace ceiling for that phase.

checkpoints.title: km 10
checkpoints.read: Right after the km 10 beep: last-lap pace + lap-avg HR.

cells.text: Great day -> hold, don't speed up
Ease to 4:45 -> B unless settled by km 13

examples.a: You're under-running with HR headroom, ~1 min behind A-real. Build to 4:38-4:40 over the next 2 km (about 5 s/km per km), no surge. Running 4:38 from here quietly wins back ~40 s by km 30. Re-check at km 13: HR 153-156 at 4:38 -> A-real. HR jumps >158 at 4:40 -> it was only low because you were slow; today is a B day, settle at 4:45-4:48.

Great sign, but do not keep 4:30. HR drifts ~4-5 bpm from km 10 to 21 at the same pace (154 now -> 158-160 at the half), 4:30 burns proportionally more glycogen than 4:36, and Sep 20 showed 4:18 early became 4:35 late at the same HR. Ease to 4:34-4:36 and tuck in behind the 3:15 pacer. Bank energy, not time.

examples.q: What if HR then rises above 158 before the half?
examples.a: Use the over-ceiling protocol: 1-2 bpm over -> ease 5 s/km and wait 1 km; 3-5 over -> ease 10 s/km; still over after 2 km -> drop one lane; >163 -> straight to B.

checkpoints.title: Half (21.1 km)
checkpoints.read: Elapsed time vs split table + last-lap pace + lap-avg HR.

examples.a: Skip the next honey sip, water only at that station, then resume the schedule. Don't double up later.

examples.q: Lost the pacer in a station scrum?
examples.a: Don't sprint back. Run your lane's pace; if HR allows you'll drift back onto them over 2-3 km.

checkpoints.title: km 30 - the real decision
checkpoints.read: Last-lap pace + lap-avg HR + body check: legs, sips 1-6 taken, stomach.

cells.text: Fuel issue? honey + banana, then build

examples.q: When am I allowed to PUSH?
examples.a: Only if ALL are true: lap-avg HR <= 160, legs OK, honey sips 1-6 taken, stomach fine. If any one is missing, read the grid one column to the right.

examples.q: Pace dropped 10+ s/km at the same HR between km 25 and 30?
examples.a: That's the Sep 26 pattern (glycogen + fluid). Survival C: next honey sip now, banana at 31.5, two cups of water, walk 10 s through stations. Keep running to the line.
HR cap off. Race the last 7.2 km. Coke at 39.5, everything you have from km 40.
Stay in your lane until km 40, then empty the tank for the last 2.2 km.
The finish line is the goal. Keep running between stations; Coke at 39.5 helps.

pacer.strategy: Start 50-100 m BEHIND the 3:15 pacer (Suunto flag, ~4:37/km even). Close the gap through km 5-15 only while HR stays <=158. HR >158 for 2 km straight while with them -> let them go (= A-real). With the group at the half at <=158 -> sit in, draft, switch off until km 30.

fueling.why: Honey is ~38% fructose and ~31% glucose. Glucose enters the gut wall through SGLT1 (caps ~60 g/h); fructose uses a separate door, GLUT5 (~30 g/h more). Together you can absorb up to ~90 g/h, but your gut has only practised ~60 g/h, so 65-70 g/h stays close to what you rehearsed.

energyBudget.note: Only if Saturday's carb-load is done (~650-800 g carbs).
Even at marathon pace ~1/4-1/3 of energy. The HR cap keeps this share high.
2 flasks (~200 g) + pre-start honey + Coke at 39.5.

flasks.name: Flask A
flasks.recipe: 85 mL honey (~120 g, 6 level tbsp) + 75 mL warm water -> ~160 mL

flasks.name: Flask B
flasks.recipe: 85 mL honey (~120 g, 6 level tbsp) + 75 mL warm water -> ~160 mL

flasks.name: Water
flasks.recipe: 500 mL plain water (optional pinch of salt only if practised)
flasks.sips: km 0-6 gap + any missed cup. Empty by ~km 25.

prep: Mix with warm water, shake hard. ~50% sugar: runny enough to squeeze at 10 °C. Pure honey won't flow through the nozzle.
Mark 4 quarter-lines on each flask with tape or marker (1 sip = 1/4 flask = ~25 g carbs).
Test-squeeze both Saturday night and Sunday morning.
fueling.sep26Lesson: Sep 26 (31.6 km): ~60 g/h of carbs on paper, but very concentrated honey + only ~420 mL/h fluid + started dehydrated (Fritz-Kola only) + midday start + no carb-load. HR drifted +18 bpm at the same easy pace from km 22 and you slumped at km 27 (~2h30). The carbs were in the vest, not in the muscles.

sips.note: 1 tbsp honey from a jar/sachet + a few sips of water

hydration.plan: A cup at EVERY station (13), ~100-150 mL each - pinch the cup into a spout, slow 2-3 s. Two cups at supply stations if you missed one. Backup: 500 mL in the vest.

estimate.label: Net deficit
estimate.value: ~1-2 L (1.3-2.5% body mass) - normal, well tolerated in the cool

stations.supplyContents: Water, bananas, Hydraid electrolyte (lemon), Dextro bars. Dextro PROLINE gels from km 26.5 (untested - emergency only). Red Bull at 10.5/31.5/37. Coke at 39.5.

settings: External HR: Polar H10 paired; close Polar Flow/Beat on the phone first (H10 holds one Bluetooth link)
Optional HR alert at 159 for the first half (ignore/raise to 166 after km 30)

racePage.use: Steering - ignore the first ~200 m after each beep
Decisions (fallback: current HR judged over ~30 s)
Compare to the split table at 10 / half / 30 / 35

watch.h10: Wet the electrodes before the start, anti-chafe under the strap, check pairing during the warm-up.

items: 15 min very easy shakeout - use it as the watch/H10 dry run (auto-lap beep, fields, HR source).
Bib pickup Olympic Park (Sat 10:00-18:00). Don't spend hours standing at the expo.
Carb-load ~650-800 g carbs (8-10 g/kg): white bread/bagels with honey & jam, juice, big rice/pasta lunch, pretzels, bananas, rice cakes, gummies. Low fibre, low fat, nothing new.
2.5-3 L fluid through the day, some salty food. Early, normal-size dinner (~18:30).
Evening: mix both honey flasks, mark quarter-lines, test-squeeze. Pin bib, lay out kit, charge watch + H10 check. Sleep early.
Breakfast ~3 h pre-start, ~150 g carbs: 2-3 white rolls/toast with honey or jam + banana + coffee. Skip the Müsli (fibre).
500 mL water with a pinch of salt, finished by ~07:15. Then only sips.
U3 to Olympiazentrum (free with bib, trains every 5 min). Bag drop in the Runner's Bag. Toilet early.
10 min easy jog + 3 strides. Wet H10, confirm pairing on the T-Rex.
In the start block (>=15 min before). 1 tbsp honey + a few sips. Find the 3:15 flag - line up 50-100 m behind it.

redFlags: Stop / medical tent (at the aid stations): chest pain, confusion, chills or stopped sweating, blurred vision.

evidence.intro: Why 3:14-3:18 and not sub-3: km-by-km Strava laps from this block. Pace at marathon-effort HR, not hope.

sessions.name: 28 km, peak long run
sessions.detail: 10 km 5:47 @136 · 6 km 4:18 @163 · 6 km 5:56 @140 · 6 km 4:35 @161.5 (max 170) - 17 s/km fade at the same effort after 22 km

conclusions: 4:20/km costs 160-164 bpm (96-98% of LT 167) - a half-marathon effort, not a marathon one.
Marathon HR for a trained runner is ~92-95% of LT = 154-159 bpm -> ~4:36-4:42/km for you once tapered.
Longest continuous MP block was 6 km; MP after 30 km is untested -> the HR cap in the first half is non-negotiable.
CTL ~45 is low for 3:15; sub-3:15 is ~35-40%, 3:15-3:18 is the honest centre.
